chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of Hanan ibn Sadeer, that one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said that he had heard him say:

Seven people who shall receive the hardest punishment on the Resurrection Day are as follows: Adam’s son who killed his brother; Nimrood who argued with Abraham about God; two of the Israelites, one of whom made the Israelites Jewish and the other one who made the Israelites Christian; the Pharaoh who said, 'I am your Lord, Most High'; and two of the followers of the Muslim nation.
ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people who receive the hardest punishment on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these seven archetypes of arrogance and deviation, starting with Qabil (Cain) and Nimrod, then the two major Jewish and Christian communities, Pharaoh, and concluding with two figures from the Muslim Ummah. This enumeration underscores the continuity of divine punishment across prophetic eras, linking the specific sins of earlier nations to potential spiritual failures within the Shia community. The inclusion of 'two from this Ummah' invites scholarly reflection on the specific traits of arrogance or deviation that mirror the earlier examples.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-16 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Hanan ibn Sadeer, that one of the companions of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said that he had heard him say, “

Seven people who shall receive the hardest punishment on the Resurrection Day are as follows: Adam’s son who killed his brother (MGB); Nimrood who argued with Abraham (MGB) about God; two of the Israelites one of whom made the Israelites Jewish and the other one who made the Israelites Christian; the Pharaoh who said, ‘I am your Lord, Most High’ ; and two of the followers of the Muslim nation.”
